description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20).  Programs: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/modwork/mw-21-*, mw-19-*, mw-05-*, mw-25-*; probes in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/.  ONE task on purpose: these are low-frequency; an agent with a free hour takes (1) and (2), which are real bugs, and turns (3)-(5) into not-supported.md citations.  (1): instrument a copy of Memoize.pm as #2080 did for File::Find -- Memoize installs with `*{$name} = $wrapper` after resolving `$name` through `caller`; suspect the caller-package resolution or its `_make_cref` symbolic lookup.  (2): lib/English.pm -- how are the aliases made (glob assignment `*LIST_SEPARATOR = *"`)?  the interpolation join reads the `$"` CELL; under Direction D an aliased scalar must share the cell (the same mechanism as #2008's exported-scalar alias -- do it after #2008).


=== CORRECTION (Fable, s500, 2026-09-28) ===
(4) is NOT the stash walk: PCL's `keys %{"Archive::Tar::Constant::"}` lists the constants (probed).  Archive::Tar::Constant::_list_consts keeps a name only when `defined prototype($sub) and not length prototype($sub)`, and run-time prototype() is undef for every `use constant` sub under PCL -> @EXPORT empty -> the row dies at the first MODE.  Filed as **#2533** (register classic prototypes + constants' '' through the existing registrar; the not-supported entry's own condition is met).  (3) probed in detail (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s500/review/tmp/sutil.pl): `isweak` is a stub (lib/Scalar/Util.pm `sub isweak { 0 }`; perl: weak after weaken, a COPY is strong, re-assignment clears it), `openhandle` answers TRUE for everything incl. a never-opened glob, a CLOSED lexical handle, undef and a plain string (#1571's stub), `readonly` answers false for a literal / a number / undef (perl 1; #1391's family).  All three are in the everyday-singles brief `~/pcl-agent-scratch/s500/s500a/prompt.md`; (1) Memoize and (2) English stay here.

=== s500a (Opus, 2026-09-30): (3) and (4) settled; (1), (2), (5) stay here ===
(4) is #2533, DONE s500a: run-time prototype() registers every definition, so Archive::Tar::Constant exports its 49 constants (= perl).  The row then met `$entry->$_()` (fixed s500a) and now stops at IO::Zlib's `tie *$fh` (#155) -- baseline row re-attributed to #155.
(3) isweak and openhandle DONE s500a (Scalar::Util shim -> builtin::is_weak / builtin::openhandle; runtime p-isweak's weak mark on the VARIABLE box, cleared by any store; p-openhandle = an OPEN stream or undef, never a name lookup) -- scratch/s500a/probes/sutil.pl rows 1-6 and 10-12 and oh.pl = perl.  readonly("lit") is NOT fixed: measured, a literal argument / a temp / an unboxed variable are the same raw CL value inside the callee; the rest is #1391 (entry in not-supported.md).  The everyday Scalar-Util row now differs ONLY at `ro`/`rw` and is re-attributed to #1391.


=== s502e (Opus, 2026-10-04): item (1) Memoize DONE -- items (2) English stays here, (5) is s501t's ===
(1) There was no Memoize-specific or caller/glob mechanism bug.  Core Memoize::_wrap is `Scalar::Util::set_prototype(sub { ...cache... }, prototype $orig)` and memoize installs that RETURN value; lib/Scalar/Util.pm's set_prototype was an empty stub (#2538), so the wrapper was the empty list and nothing was installed.  #2538's one-line shim fixes it.  Probes (scratch/s502e/p/memo1.pl, memo2.pl, bm.pl = everyday/modules/Benchmark-Memoize.pl) == perl on the rebased tree (618db500 + s502e): calls 2 (perl 2), a code ref taken BEFORE memoize still calls the original, `memoize('Pkg::f')`, a sub in another package, list context, the prototype carried over, unmemoize, flush_cache, an anonymous sub, NORMALIZER.  Everyday modules/Benchmark-Memoize `same` (row edited out).  Guard Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t rows 83-84 (inverse-verified).
(2) `local $LIST_SEPARATOR` under English is untouched by s502e (everyday modules/Sys-Hostname-Env-English still cites it).


=== s507b (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-04): item (2) DONE ===
Measured: `local $LIST_SEPARATOR` lowered to p-local-cell on English's cell, which installed a FRESH box there --
`$"` (a runtime special, localized by a dynamic let) never saw it; and `local $"` rebound the special while
English's cell still held the old box.  perl shares one GLOB (`*LIST_SEPARATOR = *"`), which PCL cannot lower.
Generic mechanism (runtime): p-local-cell and p-local-cell-if localize a TIED cell THROUGH its tie (FETCH the old
value, STORE undef, STORE the new value, STORE the saved value back at exit -- perl's sequence, probed with a
tracing tie).  Data (lib/English.pm, rule 9a): $LIST_SEPARATOR, $OUTPUT_FIELD_SEPARATOR/$OFS,
$OUTPUT_RECORD_SEPARATOR/$ORS, $SUBSCRIPT_SEPARATOR/$SUBSEP, $INPUT_RECORD_SEPARATOR/$RS and $OUTPUT_AUTOFLUSH
are TIED to their punctuation variable instead of value-aliased.  Probe scratch/s507b/m5/en.pl (local / plain
assignment / read, both directions, a called sub, a slice) identical to perl except `"[$\"]"`, a PRE-EXISTING
interpolation bug filed #2704.  everyday modules/Sys-Hostname-Env-English now `same` (row edited out of the
baseline).  Guards Pl/t/english-01.t rows 12-13 (both fail on 08de9e4f).
All five items are now settled ((1) s502e, (3)/(4) s500a, (5) s501t #155), so the task is completed.
